title: A versioned request format
description:
The echo protocol's next version sends structured requests. Each message is bytes laid out as:

| Offset | Size | Field |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | 2 | `version`, little-endian, currently 1 |
| 2 | 2 | `flags` |
| 4 | 4 | `length` of the payload that follows, little-endian |
| 8 | `length` | the payload |

Write `encode(flags, payload)`, which builds a version 1 message, and `decode(bytes)`, which parses one and returns the version, flags and payload, or `std::nullopt` if:

- the message is shorter than the 8-byte header;
- the version is not 1;
- `length` is larger than the bytes actually present after the header, or larger than `kMaxPayload` (4096);
- there are extra bytes after the payload.

Use only explicit byte arithmetic, no `memcpy` of structs (lesson 2.06).
hints: Encoding writes each field's bytes lowest first, then appends the payload.

Decoding: check the header is present, read the fields, then check the version and that `length` equals exactly the number of bytes after the header and is within the limit. Comparing with `bytes.size() - 8` (after checking the size is at least 8) cannot overflow.
